transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I came in because I'm just tired all the time. Honestly, by midmorning at work... after just reviewing some files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
Have you or anyone who sleeps near you noticed loud snoring, gasping, or pauses in your breathing while you sleep?
No, not that I know of. My husband hasn't ever mentioned anything like loud snoring or... or me stopping breathing. I don't wake up gasping or anything like that, I just always feel drained.
How many hours of sleep do you typically get at night, and do you feel rested when you wake up?

I usually get about seven or eight hours a night. But no, I don't feel rested when I wake up. It's like the sleep doesn't even do anything. I just wake up feeling just as heavy and tired as when I went to bed.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in things you normally like doing?

No, I wouldn't say so. I still like doing the things I usually enjoy. I mean... I might be too tired to actually do them sometimes because I feel so drained, but my actual interest in them hasn't really gone away.
Have you noticed any unexplained weight gain or weight loss over the past few months?
No, my weight has been pretty steady. I haven't noticed any major changes, either gaining or losing. It's just been about the same as usual.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold, having dry skin, or being more constipated than usual lately?
No, I haven't noticed any of that. I'm not unusually cold or anything, and my skin seems fine. And no issues with being constipated, either. Everything has been pretty normal with all of that.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things—more than most people would—and having trouble controlling that worry?
No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal everyday things from time to time, but not more than anyone else, I don't think. It's definitely not out of control or anything like that.
Have you noticed being unusually thirsty or needing to urinate more often than usual lately?
No, I haven't had any issues with that. My thirst is about the same as it's always been, and I haven't been going to the bathroom any more frequently than normal.
Have you noticed any shortness of breath, dizziness, or looking unusually pale, especially with physical activity?
No, I haven't experienced any of that. I'm not short of breath or dizzy, and my color seems normal. Even when I'm active, everything feels fine in that regard.

Do you find yourself actually falling asleep or needing to nap during the day, even in situations like meetings or while driving, or is it more that you feel physically and mentally worn out without actually dozing off?

It's more that I feel worn out without actually falling asleep. I don't doze off while driving or in meetings or anything like that. But honestly, that's why I came in—I'm just tired all the time. 

By midmorning at work, even after just reviewing a few files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already completely running on empty.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at night or wake up frequently during the night before your usual wake time?

No, my sleep is actually fine. I fall asleep without much trouble, and I don't really wake up during the night. I pretty much sleep straight through until my alarm goes off... I just still feel completely drained when I do.
How long have you been experiencing this constant tiredness and mental fatigue—has it been going on for several months or longer?

It's been going on for a long time... much longer than a few months. I'd say it's been about three years and three months now. It started right around the time I got moved into a role with more responsibility at work. They had me start mentoring the junior adjusters and overseeing the new workflow systems, and that's when this constant tiredness really set in.

After you push yourself physically or mentally—like a busy day at work—do you notice your fatigue and other symptoms get significantly worse for the following day or two, requiring extra time to recover?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. It doesn't seem to get worse for a day or two just because I had a heavy day at work. 

It's honestly just a constant level of tired. Whether I push myself or take it easy, I wake up the next morning feeling that exact same amount of drained. So I wouldn't say I need extra days to recover... I just never really feel recovered to begin with.
